claims.title: Inverse growth metrics and global finite-thickness realization

quoted_fields.interface: Thin Kirchhoff--Love/StVenant--Kirchhoff equal-layer model with independently programmable orthotropic layer metrics, target compatible first/second forms and sufficiently small thickness. Distinct introduced isotropic restriction and normal-thickened helicoid retain their exact scopes.
quoted_fields.failure: The primary inverse is prior machinery, not a new ROOT theorem. Six independent metric-field components per point are a physical input, not delivered by one global stimulus. Isotropic exact form-matching obstructions do not prohibit strained equilibria or other mechanisms. The helicoid counterexample does not refute a sufficiently-thin midsurface theorem.
